column2: Describe what students should know, understand, or be able to do by the end of the lesson. Objectives should be specific, measurable, and aligned with curriculum standards. They provide clear goals that inform planning, instruction, and assessment.

Outline the key concepts, facts, skills, and information that will be taught in the lesson. This includes the subject matter to be covered, any relevant background knowledge, and how it connects to prior and future learning.

Explain how the lesson will be adapted to cater for diverse learners. Include strategies for supporting different readiness levels, learning styles, and student needs. This could involve modifications to content, process, environment, or expected outcomes.

List all materials, tools, and teaching aids required for the lesson. This includes physical items (e.g., books, handouts, manipulatives), digital resources (e.g., videos, software), and any setup or preparation needed to facilitate learning.
